state:
**Goal `growth-proof`, Stage 3 should now pass; Stage 4's first slice is on disk.** No floor is carried.

The whole `bun nv scaling --iterations --sized` run on this tree (about 30 minutes) named six oversized benches and one that grows. The six were lowered with `--sized --lower`: `core/Cli/colorDepth` (2048), `core/IO/canonicalize` (512), `core/IO/isFile` (256), `core/IO/size` (256), `core/IO-File/flush` (256) and `core/IO-Metadata/isFile` (1024). A filtered `--sized` re-run of the six passes. The whole run was not repeated after the lowering. The driver's sweep is that check.

`core/Process-Handle/writeStdin` gives `grows`, `flat` or `unclear` on the same commit, because its allocations per call depend on when the blocking pool's job ends. It carries `// proof: gap nvs-host/a-blocking-call-allocates-by-when-it-ends`, and `--iterations` now counts a bench that grows and carries a marker naming an existing record as a known gap, the way `--growth` already did. That gap is owned by M10, not by this goal.

The seven `unclear` benches (`core/Http-TlsInfo/verified`, `version`, `core/IO/isReadable`, `core/IO-File/close`, `truncate`, `write`, `core/Queue/purge`) do not fail the check. Stage 6's section lists the benches the proof cannot judge.

The selection engine's `bench` atom and `recordBench` are as the last session left them: `discover` does not list benches yet, on purpose, and nothing calls `recordBench`.

The clock at the lowered N mostly reads 0. Whether to time the clock at a larger, clock-only N is the user's call, and nothing has changed for it.
